speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS experiencing decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. Given your immunocompromised state, we need to determine if this is due to an opportunistic infection like Cytomegalovirus retinitis or another cause. Are you also experiencing floaters, flashes of light, or any pain when moving your eyes?

REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmoscopy
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Photography

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ophthalmoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities with dot-blot hemorrhages are highly characteristic of retinitis in an AIDS patient. Did you notice any sudden loss of vision or "cortical blindness" in that eye recently?

REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_Fluorescein_Angiography

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis

The findings of granular yellow-white retinal opacities and hemorrhages, combined with your history of AIDS, recent fungal esophagitis, and Kaposi's sarcoma, are classic for CMV retinitis. The absence of pain further supports this diagnosis over other infectious causes like toxoplasmosis or bacterial endophthalmitis.
